speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Before I deal with the Bill proper, please allow me to outline the important roles and functions that land surveyors perform.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Land surveyors conduct land, building or property surveys in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Such surveys are necessary to demarcate property boundaries required for the issuance of titles and land development works.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: They also have the expertise to conduct other types of survey work, such as as-built, topographical and setting-out surveys.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Land surveyors play an important role in the built environment sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: By depicting accurate boundaries and areas in their cadastral surveys, land surveyors contribute to a stable and reliable property ownership framework, which gives certainty to individuals and businesses alike in their dealings.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Land surveyors also work with other professionals within the sector, including architects and professional engineers, throughout the lifecycle of a development project.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The work stretches from concept to construction and even beyond, from topographical surveys of the site to the final stage of cadastral survey when the building is completed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Conversely, any errors by land surveyors, such as in the determination of property boundaries in a cadastral survey, can have significant downstream consequences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: For example, discrepancies in the surveyed land area occupied by a property could affect the property's valuation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Errors could also lead to inaccurately demarcated boundaries, resulting in encroachments onto neighbouring plots of land owned by different parties.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The Land Surveyors Act 1991, the Act, was enacted to establish a system of registration and regulate the qualifications and practices of land surveyors who supply their services in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Under the Act, the Land Surveyors Board (LSB) oversees the registration of land surveyors, regulation of the qualifications and practice of land surveyors, as well as related matters.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: LSB is also empowered by the Act to establish, maintain and develop the standard of professional conduct and ethics of the surveying profession.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Under our current framework, individuals, regardless of nationality, can only engage in land survey work in Singapore, if they are registered surveyors who have a valid practising certificate issued by LSB; authorised surveyors; or carrying out land survey work under the direction or supervision of such registered surveyors or authorised surveyors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Registered surveyors are individuals who are registered as land surveyors under section 12 of the Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: These individuals must meet LSB's eligibility criteria, such as passing of examinations and a professional interview conducted by LSB.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Authorised surveyors refer to land surveyors employed by the Singapore Land Authority, regardless of whether they are registered under section 12 of the Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This framework has served Singapore well over the years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: It has ensured that all land surveyors providing services in Singapore are fit and qualified to do so.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: At the same time, land surveying is evolving, for example, to include the use of rapidly developing land surveying technologies, such as ground penetrating radar.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This is creating new and exciting opportunities for cross-border exchange of expertise.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Given these developments, we are introducing this Bill to help the local profession to pursue these opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: I will take hon Members through these areas in turn.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: First, the amendments to facilitate the implementation of MRAs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: It also allows Singapore to benefit from the expertise of foreign land surveyors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: MRAs will also allow us to build up and strengthen new capabilities within the local surveying profession, through the mutual exchange of knowledge, expertise and best practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: For example, registered foreign surveyors may be able to share their experience or expertise with specialised equipment in emerging areas like aerial Light Detection and Ranging (LIDAR) scanning, underground survey and large-scale mapping.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Our local registered surveyors can also benefit by collaborating with registered foreign surveyors who have access to specialised equipment, such as cameras used to conduct aerial mapping.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This can help them to take on new or different types of projects, with lower upfront capital investment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Hon Members who are familiar with the developments in the built environment sector will know that land surveyors, architects and professional engineers are often collectively referred to as allied professionals.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Members may also access the handout through the MP@SGPARL App.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: As set out on page 1 of the handout, currently, a local registered surveyor who wishes to engage in land survey work overseas is likely to have to go through the full qualification process to be registered to practise in that jurisdiction.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The surveyor will have to meet that jurisdiction's requirements, including residency or citizenship-based restrictions, if applicable.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The application process may also involve steps, such as passing examinations or professional interviews conducted by the overseas Board or Authority.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: However, where there is an MRA in place, the local registered surveyor can apply to LSB to be recognised for the purposes of the MRA instead.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: After the ASEAN MRA is implemented, the ASEAN Registered Surveyor Scheme, the Scheme, will be introduced.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Eligible land surveyors can apply through their local survey authorities to the ASEAN Competent Authority Committee on Surveying (ACACS) to be recognised as ASEAN registered surveyors.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Such ASEAN registered surveyors will not have to go through the full qualification process in that country but will remain subject to any conditions imposed by the relevant overseas survey board or authority.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This will help our local registered surveyors to tap on business opportunities in different markets and broaden their exposure and experience.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The ASEAN member states have been working together to implement the Scheme.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: LSB will update the local registered surveyor community, when the Scheme is ready for implementation.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Next, turning to page 2 of the handout, such MRAs will also introduce a new way for foreign land surveyors to contribute to land survey work in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Aside from the three existing pathways through which individuals can engage in survey work in Singapore, which I touched on earlier, foreign land surveyors will be able to apply to LSB to be registered foreign surveyors.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This will allow them to engage in survey work in Singapore in a manner permitted by LSB pursuant to an MRA.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: For example, under the Scheme, ASEAN registered surveyors from other ASEAN member states will be able to collaborate with our local registered surveyors on surveying projects in Singapore, after they are registered with LSB.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: These registered foreign surveyors will not be allowed to practise independently.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: They can only do so in collaboration with a local registered surveyor.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: On the matter of safeguards in the implementation of MRAs, I wish to highlight that foreign land surveyors will need to meet certain requirements before they can provide land surveying services in Singapore in accordance with the terms of an MRA.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: For example, under the Scheme, there will be binding minimum requirements in terms of qualifications and work experience, which individuals must meet before they can be recognised as ASEAN registered surveyors.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The new section 12A(4) inserted by clause 9 of the Bill also allows LSB to impose additional conditions on foreign land surveyors as part of their registration as registered foreign surveyors.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This enables LSB to ensure there are safeguards to protect the interests of the public, where required, and allows it to continue to effectively regulate the quality of land surveying services provided in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Registered foreign surveyors will support, rather than compete with, our local registered surveyors.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: For example, as mentioned earlier, foreign ASEAN registered surveyors will not be allowed to provide land surveying services independently in Singapore, that is, without a local partner.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: If they wish to practise independently in Singapore, they must go through the same process as any other individual who wishes to be a local registered surveyor today.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This includes passing the examinations and professional interview conducted by LSB, being registered with LSB and having in force a practising certificate.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: LSB will continue to monitor the implementation of the Scheme in Singapore and make adjustments where necessary.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I now move to the second proposal in the Bill, the introduction of official titles for local registered surveyors and registered foreign surveyors.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This will grant greater recognition to local registered surveyors and help distinguish local registered surveyors from their counterparts.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Under section 10(2) as amended by clause 6, local registered surveyors will be able to use the title "RS".

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This is similar to the use of professional titles amongst registered architects and registered professional engineers.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Registered foreign surveyors will be able to use a separate designation to be determined by LSB.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The final proposal in the Bill is to update the fines and penalties for illegal practice and improper conduct in land surveying.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: It is thus timely to review them to ensure they remain effective deterrents going forward.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: LSB carried out a holistic review, referencing similar offences in the Architects Act 1991 and the Professional Engineers Act 1991, while keeping in mind the difference in the nature of the work of land surveyors and that of these allied professionals.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: For specific offences, such as illegal practice, wilful falsification of register and wrongly procuring registration, stiffer fines are proposed.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: LSB is empowered to impose these penalties on (a) registered surveyors and (b) licensed corporations/partnerships/limited liability partnerships respectively, in cases where LSB considers that no cause of sufficient gravity for cancellation of a registration, suspension from practice or revoking a licence exists but some form of disciplinary action is appropriate.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This pertains to a refusal or failure, when required to do so by LSB or an Investigation Committee convened by LSB, to give evidence, answer truthfully and fully any question or produce any book, document or paper.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: These will make clear that the term "registered surveyor", when used in these other Acts, only applies to the land surveyors registered under section 12 of the Land Surveyors Act, that is, to local registered surveyors.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This will avoid any confusion with the introduction of registered foreign surveyors into the local land surveying landscape.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: In closing, Sir, these amendments will make it easier for local registered surveyors to tap on opportunities overseas and, at the same time, allow Singapore to tap on external land surveying expertise and resources to support the built environment sector.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: They will also provide strong recognition for practising local registered surveyors on par with their allied counterparts, such as architects and professional engineers.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This will allow it to continue upholding the standing and integrity of the professional land survey fraternity in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I appreciate the Ministry's efforts to elevate and integrate Singapore's surveying profession within the ASEAN framework.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The proposed amendments, particularly those facilitating the ASEAN MRA and the introduction of the ASEAN ARS, hold significant potential for strengthening the profession in Singapore and the region.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: However, while the Bill aims to enhance the mutual recognition of land surveyors within ASEAN, I have several clarifications on the Bill.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The Bill seeks to amend the Land Surveyors Act 1991.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Why has there been such a notable delay in finalising the MRA?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Is it prudent to implement this Bill when the details of the scheme remain unclear?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Without the finalised details, how can we ensure that the mutual recognition arrangement will be beneficial and fair to our local surveyors?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Second, Mr Speaker, Sir, I would like to ask about the potential impact of this Bill on our local surveying professionals.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We should support the vision of a more integrated ASEAN surveying landscape.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Nonetheless, we must ensure that our local surveyors are not inadvertently disadvantaged by this process.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Opening our market to ASEAN-based surveyors raises several concerns.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If not, by being the first, will Singapore inadvertently disadvantage our local surveyors?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The possibility of lower-cost ASEAN-based surveyors competing for jobs in Singapore could negatively impact the livelihoods of our local professionals.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I urge the Ministry to clarify what measures are in place to protect our surveyors from unfair competition and ensure a level playing field.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Furthermore, the principle of reciprocity must be carefully examined.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Our local surveyors will be required to register with LSB to perform work overseas under this scheme.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Yet, are our ASEAN counterparts equally prepared to accept Singaporean surveyors?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will our professionals face any red tape, bureaucratic hurdles or barriers in these foreign jurisdictions hindering their ability to compete for projects fairly overseas?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Clarity on these reciprocal arrangements is essential to ensure that this Bill truly fosters mutually beneficial professional mobility within ASEAN.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Do we know of any other ASEAN jurisdictions which may be implementing such an arrangement soon?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Third, Mr Speaker, Sir, we need to uphold the highest standards of professional practice within the Singaporean surveying sector.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: While we seek greater regional collaboration, we should never compromise on the quality of surveying work conducted within our nation.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: To maintain these high standards, it is essential to ensure that foreign surveyors entering our market are adequately qualified and their work meet our stringent requirements.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How will we ensure that ASEAN-based surveyors possess the necessary qualifications and competencies for the scope of work required in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will there be stringent and transparent verification processes in place to validate their credentials and ensure equivalence with our local standards?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Moreover, I believe it is critical to address the issue of quality assurance.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will the work of foreign surveyors be subject to rigorous oversight by our local registered surveyors?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: To guarantee accountability and maintain the highest levels of professional rigour, should we consider mandating that a local registered surveyor co-signs the work of foreign surveyors engaged in projects within Singapore?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Should there be any dispute on the work of these foreign surveyors, what recourse do potential clients have?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Have we conducted a comprehensive impact assessment to fully understand how local surveyors and businesses, particularly smaller firms, will be affected by the increased competition?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If so, how will we address them to ensure consistent, high-quality survey work across borders when projects involve professionals from different nations?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Maintaining our standards of precision and accuracy necessitates a clear understanding of how we will navigate these potential differences.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Given that laws, regulations and even established methodologies can vary among countries, should we consider mandating that ASEAN surveyors, before practising here, undertake a mandatory familiarisation programme?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This programme could focus on Singapore-specific surveying regulations, legal precedents and common practices.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Additionally, Mr Speaker, Sir, are the instruments and technologies used in other ASEAN nations directly compatible with our own standards and systems?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If not, how do we ensure uniformity and accuracy when integrating data collected using potentially disparate methodologies?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Should foreign surveyors be required to utilise equipment that aligns with Singapore's standards while operating here?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This, again, highlights the need for a comprehensive integration process, perhaps through the mandatory familiarisation programme I proposed earlier.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In a small and densely populated nation like ours, where land is an invaluable and finite resource, the role of land surveyors is critical.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They are the guardians of our boundaries, ensuring the precise demarcation of every square metre.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Their meticulous work underpins our property ownership records, our construction projects and even the management of our underground infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The very foundation of our built environment relies upon the expertise of our land surveyors.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Only through careful consideration, thorough planning and a commitment to transparency can we ensure that this Bill achieves its intended goals of regional integration, without compromising the interests of our local surveying professionals.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: First, on the timing and rationale of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The hon Member is right to observe that it has been about 17 years since the Framework Arrangement was signed in 2007.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This reflects the complexity of the task at hand.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: We had to deal with the unique characteristics of jurisdictions across ASEAN and, of course, the domestic legislation dealing with boundary and geographical locations of the various properties as well.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: In addition, there is a need to strike a balance between greater ease of movement for land surveyors and also meeting local requirements.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: So, all these led to the time that has been taken.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: But the passing of this Bill is an important milestone because it is an indication that we are turning the corner and, hopefully, we will be able to get the details of the Scheme, as commonly agreed amongst the ASEAN member states.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: So, this is a safeguard to make sure that at any one point in time there would be reciprocity between member states.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: So, that is one big safeguard which will address some of the concerns that were raised by the hon Member just now.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The next area which I want to touch on is the issue of timing.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: As I said in my speech, LSB would be making announcements on the details of the Scheme as and when they are ready.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Moving to the second area for clarification, the impact on local surveyors.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The first point to note, as I mentioned earlier, is that the MRA would only be put into effect when other member states are ready.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: So, we ensure that the benefits are reciprocal.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: In other words, when they do the work and they sign off, it is not enough for the registered foreign surveyors to sign off.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The local registered surveyors would have to sign off as well and this is a good safeguard, the reason being, with the local registered surveyors in play, we will be able to ensure that the local registered surveyor community would generally benefit because otherwise they would not employ registered foreign surveyors, and this is also to ensure the level of standard that is required in relation to any survey services that have been contracted.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: As far as qualifications and standards are concerned, which is the third area that the hon Member has raised, he will be happy to note that we are ad idem, we also agree that there must be a high standard of qualifications as well as experience before a registered foreign surveyor is allowed to practise in Singapore in collaboration with a local registered surveyor.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: So, this is where LSB has to come up with the criteria.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Commonly, the ASEAN Competent Authority Committee on Surveying would stipulate the minimum qualifications and experience that a registered foreign surveyor must possess before seeking to admit itself in the jurisdiction of another member state.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I now come to some of the additional points that the hon Member made in his speech.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: First, he asked whether there was a study on the potential economic implications.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: As I said in my speech, this initiative was really promulgated at the instance of LSB, which includes of members from the private sector.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: So, they are all looking forward to it and I also mentioned that allied professionals, such as professional engineers and architects, have already been subject to MRAs and they are benefiting from it as well.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Singapore remains a little red dot and we can see that with the MRA, our land surveyors have the potential to practise across jurisdictions.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Certainly, what we have here is the prospect of having in place an ASEAN MRA and that is something which I am sure they will look forward to.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The hon Member also mentioned about the prospect of standardising the methodology standards for surveys and that is a fair point.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: But one would have to put in place the MRA first and then work and endeavour towards standardisation.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: At this point in time, one good safeguard is the fact that a registered foreign surveyor has to collaborate with a local registered surveyor so that the local standards would be observed.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This is important, given the shrinking manpower pool, the increasing use of technology in the field and the emergence of new focus areas in the industry.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: All of these mean that it will no longer be sufficient for our local registered surveyors to be proficient only in the traditional domains of land surveying.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: It is thus critical that we take advantage of new areas of opportunities to pivot and launch the profession to even greater heights and be ready for future challenges.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Any clarifications for the Minister of State, Mr Yip?
